title: A New Era of World Finance: The Strategy For A Global Decentralized Digital Financial Market

context_sources.name: Barrdear and Kumhof, Bank of England working paper 605
Qian Yao, economic effects of legal digital currency, 2019
HM Treasury, UK national risk assessment of money laundering
Heritage Foundation and Wall Street Journal, Index of Economic Freedom

limitations: Equation numbering skips (32) and the goods-clearing identity is unnumbered.
First-order conditions of all four sectors are stated but never shown.
The score functions f, F and G in the classifier are never specified.
Beta is given as 0.971 in the prose and 0.7 in the calibration table.

tasks: Build a workable global digital financial system
Find the factors behind access, growth, security and stability
Forecast the long-run effect on banking, growth and relations

section_map.summary: Three phases: DSGE feasibility, PCA factors plus a KNN risk check, SAR spillovers.
No single currency, no forced abandonment, central bank only.
Four sectors, three holding shares, full replacement closest to the data.
Fourteen indicators to four named components, 80.2 percent.
Three regulatory paths, the third chosen, then a classifier.
Letter urging early issuance and neighbour-to-neighbour spread.

contributions.summary: A free holding share, so full replacement is tested rather than assumed.
A held-out real label used to certify the classifier.
The direct effect removed before the spillover is claimed.

dependency_graph.handoff: The feasibility result raises the question of what governs adoption
Security and access factors motivate the laundering-risk check
The issuance decision is the shock whose spillover the spatial model traces

assumptions.summary: No common currency, no forced abandonment, central bank is the only issuer.
No foreign reserves and no trade.
Distance between capitals stands in for all unobserved links.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: LIBOR near 3 percent, World Bank consumption share near 80 percent.
UK 2015 risk assessment, twelve areas, four scores.

models.summary: Four-sector DSGE with a free digital holding share.
k nearest neighbours on four risk scores.
Spatial autoregression with a Tunisia counterfactual.

verification.summary: Steady state matched to a 15 percent reserve ratio and an 80 percent consumption share.
Each parameter moved 10 percent, conclusions unchanged.
Spillover rerun at 5 percent, sign unchanged.

results_trace.summary: Full replacement: reserve ratio 17.8 percent, consumption 75 percent of output.
Digital currency classified low, probability 1, matching the label.
Indirect effects mostly positive across 163 countries.

writing_logic.summary: A cited model is corrected for one unrealistic assumption before use.
An omitted factor is given a direction of bias rather than ignored.
The direct effect is excluded so only the spillover is discussed.

language_observations.summary: A source dismissed for deviating from reality, then repaired.
A model cleared by sitting close to published ratios.
Three options set out, the third taken with a reason.
A difference of two solutions read as an indirect effect.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1: flowchart of the four tasks.
Figure 2: consumption and output after a digital currency shock.
Figure 3: twelve areas projected to two dimensions.
Figure 4: decision regions at k=3, digital currency inside the low region.
Figure 5: indirect effect on three indices after a 10 percent Tunisia shock.
Figure 6: the same indirect effect at a 5 percent shock.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Matching a steady state to two published ratios is the whole feasibility case.
One correctly classified held-out point is treated as proof of accuracy.
Tunisia's index rise is assumed to come from the currency, which the spillover inherits.

weaknesses.summary: First-order conditions are never shown, so the steady states cannot be reproduced.
Beta is 0.971 in the text and 0.7 in the table.
The score functions are unnamed, so the classifier inputs cannot be rebuilt.

independent_extensions.summary: Derive and report the first-order conditions the text omits.
Reconcile the two values of beta and rerun the steady state.
Specify f, F and G so the twelve vectors can be reproduced.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Judge adoption by matching a model's steady state to published ratios.
Issue first, then let neighbours follow, since the spillover decays with distance.

unresolved_questions.question: What are the first-order conditions behind Table 3?
What functions produce the four risk scores?
